newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wheat follows higher trend on weather fears.
newsitem.headline: German wheat follows higher trend on weather fears.

text.p: German wheat sellers marked up prices in line with sharply higher levels elsewhere in Europe, where drought fears have boosted new crop prices, brokers said on Tuesday.
This has put off domestic consumers but German material may gain a competitive advantage if drought fears persist and other origins become even more expensive, they said.
While western European countries urgently need rain over the next week to avoid damage to the crops for harvest in three months time, Germany's weather has been cool, but wet enough.
Both new crop and old crop sales were very slow but the milling industry was expected to be back in the market in May to fill some remaining gaps in its cover ahead of the harvest.
Brokers also reported German feed wheat sales to the Netherlands and Belgium, where consumers feel soymeal prices are too high for maximum inclusion in feed rations.

The Hamburg grain exchange this week raised its spot bread wheat price (12.5 percent, 220 Hagberg) by 2.50 marks to 282.50 marks a tonne free Hamburg and also raised the spot feed wheat price by 2.50 marks to 277.50.
Fob Baltic sellers raised April delivery wheat by between 1.50 and 12.50 mark per tonne on the week.
They quoted 12 percent protein wheat at 282.50-300 marks and material with 13/14 percent protein in a 290-320 mark range after 287.50-309 last week.
Fob Baltic barley was up by 1.50-2.50 at 264-287.50, steadied by recent export approvals. Fob feed rye sellers were steadier at 262.50-270 marks, depending on shipment sizes.
